7.0: A NEW KING AROSE OVER EGYPT, ETC.  Even though there was certainly a recording of this in the royal chronicles, specifically with respect to the new legislation that he enacted, the possibility did not occur to the new king of his being from this people, or that it would be appropriate to accord recognition to his people on his account.

9.0: (1) LET US DEAL SHREWDLY WITH THEM.  To move against them indirectly.
9.1: (2) THEY MAY RISE FROM THE GROUND. On their own, without us forcing them and without an obvious cause, thereby giving us a bad image before the world.  And this will happen LEST THEY INCREASE, AND IT WILL BE WHEN WAR OCCURS -- when the evils and troubles of any war, as (II Sam. 13:39), "and David pined away" -- David's soul.
9.2: (3) THEY MAY JOIN OUR ENEMIES.  For, being distinguished from us, by circumcision, by language, and by the mores of the Hebrews, such that (Gen. 43:32), "the Egyptians could not dine with the Hebrews," they are doubtless like enemies to us, and their hatred will be revealed at the time of the troubles of war.

13.0: THEY EMBITTERED THEIR LIVES.  When they kept sinning, in their mores and in their actions, as the prophet testified, saying (Ezek. 20:8), "But they defied Me and refused to listen to Me. They did not cast away the detestable things they were drawn to, nor did they give up the fetishes of Egypt. Then I resolved to pour out My fury upon them, to vent all My anger upon them there, in the land of Egypt," and accordingly, the hand of their foes was on them, with increasing severity.

1.0: I AM ADONAI.  Who sustains the existing world.  Who does not only cause it to come into existence, but also sustains it.  For the existing things do not have any being or endurance other than what I bestow on them, as it says (Neh. 9:6), "You keep them all alive."  And from this it necessarily follows that no existing being continues to exist other than My will.

2.0: (1) I APPEARED.  In a vision, which is prior to prophecy, as with (Gen. 18:1), "Adonai appeared to him."
2.1: (2) AS EL SHADDAI.  Which indicates that I caused all of existence to come into being, as is explained in Parashat Lech L'cha.
2.2: (3) BUT MY NAME ADONAI, I DID NOT MAKE MYSELF KNOWN TO THEM.  The "as" of "as El Shaddai" extends to "My name"; He said, "and _as_ My name Adonai I did not make Myself known to them in that vision.  And I did not alter any natural aspect of the unchanging elements of the world.  And thus, it is appropriate for Me to make their descendants aware of this [My nature as Adonai], for they did not receive this from their ancestors, so that I can establish them to Me as a people, and thereby redeem them.

3.0: I ALSO ESTABLISHED MY COVENANT.  And a second cause of their redemption is the covenant that I made with their ancestors.

4.0: (1) I HAVE ALSO HEARD.  And the third cause of the redemption is that I have heard their moaning and their prayers in their distress.
4.1: (2) AND I HAVE REMEMBERED MY COVENANT.  And in this way, they showed themselves fit for Me to remember My covenant, as with (Ps. 106:44-45), "Upon seeing that they were in distress, and on His hearing their cry, He recalled His covenant."

5.0: (1) THEREFORE, SAY TO THE ISRAELITES, "I AM ADONAI."  For all these three causes, say to the Israelites, that I am the one who provides existence, who makes all existing things continue in their existence, and through this power, I will bring them out, for I will alter the nature of some of them [the existing things].
5.1: (2) I WILL BRING YOU OUT FROM UNDER THE SUFFERINGS OF EGYPT.  From the day when the plagues begin to occur, the servitude will end.
5.2: (3) AND I WILL DELIVER. On the day of Raamses, when you leave their territory.
5.3: (4) AND I WILL REDEEM.  By drowning the Egyptians in the sea, as it testifies, saying, "Adonai delivered [Israel] that day." For after the death of the enslavers, they were no longer runaway slaves.

6.0: (1) I WILL TAKE YOU TO BE MY PEOPLE.  At the standing at Mt. Sinai.
6.1: (2) AND KNOW.  Recognize and digest mentally that all of this will be confirmed, as in (Deut. 11:2, 7), "Take thought this day that it was not your children, [who did not experience God, ... but you, whose eyes saw the great deeds that God performed]."
6.2: (3) THAT I, ADONAI, AM YOUR GOD WHO BRINGS OUT.  For in My being your God, looking out for you in particular, and I, the One Who brings out, strive now to bring you out, there is no doubt that I shall do everything that I have said.

8.0: (1) THEY WOULD NOT LISTEN TO MOSHE.  To mentally absorb all of this, so that they would trust in God's (may He be blessed) salvation, and He would consider it to their merit, as [He did] with Avraham.  That is why "I will give it to you" was not fulfilled through them; instead, it was given to their children.
8.1: (2) BECAUSE OF CRUSHED SPIRITS.  For their spirit was not true to God [see Ps. 78:8], and they could not absorb this mentally.
8.2: (3) AND HARD LABOR.  For were it not for the hard labor, they would have paid attention to Moshe's words, and they would have understood from his claims that it was appropriate to have faith.

0.0: (1) BECAUSE I HAVE HARDENED HIS HEART.  Even though Moshe had said (Exod. 9:30),  "I know that you do not yet have awe of Adonai," he thought that even if he does not humble himself to God from awe of God's greatness, at least he will do what God says when he can no longer withstand the evil of the plagues. He had arrived at this conclusion when he saw that it was because of the power of the plagues that he said "Adonai is the Just One." However, when he saw that, despite all this, he did  not heed, Moshe came to the conclusion that the warning was futile, for he did not listen even when he could not withstand the plagues.  Therefore, Adonai said to him, "Even though he has now also hardened his heart, I had already hardened his heart in connection with the boils (9:12).  And this was in order to multiply the signs in the midst of Egypt, so that some of them would repent and do tshuvah, and so that Israel would recount through the generations and will recognize My greatness and My benevolence.  Therefore, the warning is appropriate even though Par'oh will not heed it.
0.1: (2) THAT I MAY DISPLAY THESE MY SIGNS AMONG THEM.  So that, through them, the people will recognize my greatness and will repent of its evil.

1.0: (1) SO THAT YOU MAY RECOUNT.  So that the generations of Israel will know all this.
1.1: (2) AND SO THAT YOU MAY KNOW.  You, and your generations, and the Egyptians.

2.0: HOW LONG WILL YOU REFUSE.  Since you are not surrendering even now that you have seen my power over the surrounding atmosphere, without which you cannot live for even a moment, one can't expect you to repent from the force of any great plague, but perhaps you will repent from the force of their persistence over a long time.  Thus, it's appropriate to ask what length of time would be the limit of the persistence of your refusal with the persistence of the plagues.

4.0: THEY SHALL EAT AWAY ALL YOUR TREES.  It will ruin it, as (Deut. 31:17), "it will be ready prey," and (Ps. 79:7) "it has devoured Jacob."

9.0: (1) THE SAME AS I MEAN TO LET YOUR DEPENDENTS GO WITH YOU.  All the more so [will I not free] your livestock.
9.1: (2)  CLEARLY, YOU ARE BENT ON MISCHIEF.  Look, you are going, in this affair of yours, to what is a bad end for you, and you will meet that end, as with (Gen. 25:32), "I am at the point of death" and (Prov. 5:5), "Her feet go down to Death," and like [the Sages'] words, "they rush to the pit of destruction."

11.0: OVER THE LAND OF EGYPT FOR THE LOCUSTS.  On the locust side, that being the south side, as if commanding the locusts to come, as with (Isa. 5:26), "[God] will raise an ensign to a nation, Whistle to one at the end of the earth.There it comes with lightning speed."

15.0: PAR'OH HURRIED.  Before the locusts could consume the roots of the wheat, the spelt, and the other vegetation.

1.0: From here on, the months belong to you to do with them as you wish.  But during the days of slavery, your days were not your own but rather were for the work of others according to their will.   Therefore this [Nisan - the month of your freedom going out of Egypt] will be the first of the months of the year for you.

16.0: (1) NOW ON THE LETTING GO ... GOD DID NOT LEAD THEM BY WAY OF THE LAND OF THE PHILISTINES.  Even though the original divine intent had been to guide Israel to Mt. Sinai to receive the Torah and from there to the Land of Israel, as He said (Exod. 6:7-9), "And I will take you to be My people, ... and I will bring you into the land," still, the intent now was to guide them to the Sea of Reeds, which was not the way to either of these [Mt. Sinai or the Land of Israel], and this in order to drown Par'oh and his army, in the manner of (Jud. 4:7), "'And I will draw Sisera, toward you up to the Wadi Kishon; and I will deliver him into your hands.'"   Now the direct and short route from Egypt to the Sea of Reeds was by way of the Philistine territory, and it says that God, may He be blessed, did not want to lead them by that path --
16.1: (2) BECAUSE [JPS: ALTHOUGH] IT WAS NEARER.  Because that route and its end were close to Egypt, there would be many travelers there, and they would tell [the news] from there to Egypt and from Egypt to there --
16.2: (3) AND WHEN THEY SEE WAR. When they hear that Par'oh is preparing himself to pursue them, THE PEOPLE WILL HAVE A CHANGE OF HEART certainly out of fear of their war, and they will return to Egypt, and therefore He diverted them to a route where people did not go.

2.0: THE WILDERNESS HAS CLOSED IN ON THEM.  Ba'al Tzefon has closed the wilderness in on them.

4.0: (1) THAT THE PEOPLE HAD FLED.  That they had not gone into the wilderness on a straight line, as they had planned in saying (Exod. 8:23), "we must go a distance of three days into the wilderness," but had turned around like people fleeing without knowing the way.
4.1: (2) PAR'OH HAD A CHANGE OF HEART.  Because he thought that Ba'al Tzefon was a match for God, may He be blessed.
4.2: (3) WHAT IS THIS WE HAVE DONE, RELEASING ISRAEL.  And we did not petition Ba'al Tzefon, who would have helped us, and we would not have had to let them go.

8.0: THE EGYPTIANS GAVE CHASE TO THEM.  To those who went out defiantly.

9.0: PAR'OH CAUSED TO DRAW NEAR [JPS: AS PHARAOH DREW NEAR]. The mass force of all the Egyptian chariots.

10.0: YOU BROUGHT US TO DIE IN THE WILDERNESS.  For even if Par'oh and his army had not challenged us, just by their standing in front of us guarding the way to sustenance we will die in the wilderness from (Deut. 28:48) hunger, thirst, nakedness, and lacking everything.

14.0: (1) WHY DO YOU CRY OUT TO ME?  He [Moshe] was indeed included in the general statement (v.10) that "the Israelites cried out to Adonai," but Moshe's cry was not out of fear of Par'oh and his forces, for he had already told Israel about the downfall of Egypt and their death, in saying (vv.13-14), "you will never see them again. Adonai will battle for you."  Rather, his cry was against the Israelite leaders and their effrontery in saying (v.11), "Was it for want of graves," and he thought that, because of this, they would not heed him to enter the sea.  Therefore, He said to him, "Why do you cry out to me" about this, for you are casting suspicion on righteous people.
14.1: (2) TELL THE ISRAELITES TO GO FORWARD.  And they will not disobey you.

3.1: And how I bore you on eagles' wings - a novel way, that no one had gone through before, just like the eagle that takes care of its young in the height of the sky, where there is no other type of bird, and this is to distinguish you from all the other peoples and their pursuits, to be for Me.

4.2: And you will be a treasure among all peoples - even though all types of humans are important to me above all the lower beings, since He is represented only in them, as say Hazal (Avot): 'Humans are beloved because they were created in the Image' - still, you will be treasured among them
4.3: ...Because Mine is all the earth - and the difference between you exists in smaller or bigger amounts, despite the fact that the whole earth is Mine, and the Righteous of the Nations are important to Me without a doubt.

12.1: 2 el mot "robar també inclou el fet de "robar" éssers humans. Fins i tot enganyar a persones de forma deliberada s'anomena "robar" גנבת דעת הבריות, “robar les ments de la gent, confonent-los i fer-los creure que les mentides són veritat".

5.0: לא תטה משפט אביונך, an example of being lenient with one category of person and harsh with another. When litigants are facing you, you must not take account of any differences in their social standing. Not only this, if one of the litigants is standing during the proceedings whereas the other one is seated, this is already a form of inadmissible discrimination.

20.3: כי שמי בקרבו, "since my name is in him", and he doesn't have the power to wave My (God's) honor.

21.0: כי אם שמוע תשמע, My relationship to you then will not be protective, defensive, i.e. that I need to protect you, but aggressive, by treating your enemies as My enemies. This is the reverse of G’d’s attitude to Nineveh in Jonah 4,11 where G’d asked Jonah: “how can I not relate protectively to a city of over 120.000 people?”

1.0: דבר אל בני ישראל ויקחו לי תרומה, tell the stewards of Israel that I desire that they should collect a contribution for Me. [the Torah had not specified “who” should take. Ed.] Moses also issued such instructions on his return from the mountain the third time as the Torah reports (Exodus 34,32) ואחרי כן נגשו כל בני ישראל, ויצום את כל אשר דבר ה' אתו בהר סיני, “after that all the people of Israel drew near, and he commanded them all that the Lord had talked about with him on Mount Sinai.” This was followed by ויאמר משה אל כל עדת בני ישראל קחו מאתכם תרומה in 35,4. The עדת בני ישראל who were to carry out this “taking (accepting) of the gifts were the Sanhedrin, the High Court. The Israelites were so anxious to contribute that they did not wait until the High Court organised all this, but they approached Moses personally bringing with them so many contributions that Moses was forced to call a halt to this (36,5). This was also the reason that there was nothing left for the princes of Israel (the tribal chiefs) to contribute other than the gemstones for Aaron’s breastplate and the various oils making up the “oil of anointing.”
1.1: מאת כל איש, G’d commanded that the procedure should not be like the imposition of every man’s contribution for the public charity fund which was treated as a tax. Contributions were to be accepted only from volunteers.

19.0: (1) YOU SHALL INSTRUCT.  In what was said up to now, "You shall make," it was to be understood that he would do this through someone else, that is, that he should instruct the craftspeople to make them.  Thus, as to these three mitzvot that He commanded here, He said "And you," to inform him that he should do these himself -- that he should instruct Israel regarding the making of the oil, that he should bring Aharon and his sons close to him, and that he should speak to all of the skilled craftspeople.
19.1: (2) THAT THEY SHOULD BRING TO YOU.  As needed.  This would occur upon depletion of the oil for lighting that they were now donating, in the offerings for the Tabernacle, so that people should not think that the commandment of the lighting of the lamp would be a temporary commandment, with only that oil that had been donated.

1.0: (1) FOR HONOR (JPS: DIGNITY).  For the honor of God, may He be blessed, they being sacral garments for His worship.  (2) FOR ADORNMENT.  So that the kohen would be a teacher, awesome over all about him, they being his students, inscribed on his heart and on his shoulders.

2.0: (1) SPEAK TO ALL THE CRAFTSPEOPLE.  That they should do all that is mentioned above.
2.1: (2) TO MAKE AHARON'S GARMENTS.  That they should also make Aharon's garments.
2.2: (3) TO CONSECRATE HIM.  They should make the garments specifically for that purpose.

23.0: AND A HIN OF OLIVE OIL.  Undoubtedly, this small amount of oil did not suffice to anoint the whole amount of spices, but they would cook the oil with the water in which the spices were cooked, or they would put the oil on the surface of that cooking water, until the water was exhausted by the cooking, either by cooking or by the lesser heat from within the water, and the oil would remain, like "the product of the expert spice blenders" (v.25).  In this regard, there is a disagreement between our Sages whether there was enough [oil] to cook it with the cooking water, or whether to put the oil on the surface of the cooking water and to melt it with the steam through the lesser heat.
1. "And I said to them, "Who has gold?" "I placed this before thing to prevent, because they would not have the gold ready.
23.1: 2. "Take it off and give it to me."  "And they volunteered the gold quickly."
23.2: 3. And I cast it into the fire. "I asked for this to delay the matter and I cast it into the fire as a ruse for the goldsmiths who were needed to melt the calf."

4.0: (10 TAKE FROM YOU.  Choose persons to receive "from you the offering to Adonai."   (2) EVERYONE WHOSE HEART IS SO MOVED.  The collectors shall not go and collect it by force.  (3) SHALL BRING IT -- GIFTS FOR ADONAI.  Shall bring the freewill offering with that offering to Adonai that is not freewill, that being the offering of the half-shekel per head (Exod. 38:26).

20.0: (1) THESE ARE THE ITEMS [JPS: RECORDS] OF THE TABERNACLE.  Each of the components of the Tabernacle that are recorded above [in Parashat VaYak'hel] are the "p'kudim" about which it is said (Num. 4:32-33), "you shall list by name the objects that are their porterage tasks ... under the direction of Itamar."  And this is because each of them was worthy to be considered and to be called by name in its individual capacity and not only as part of this category.  This is all the more correct with respect to the sacred utensils in the porterage responsibility of the Kehatites.  For this reason, they did not deteriorate, as they [the Sages] said (Sukk. 45b), "Lest you say that [after the secreting of the Tabernacle] their hope is lost and their prospect is abolished, the verse states: 'Acacia wood, standing' -- they stand forever and for all time."  Also, none of them fell into the enemy's hands, by contrast to what happened with the Temple of Shlomo and its vessels, as is made clear in the destruction of the First Temple by Nevuzaradan, for there is no mention there [e.g., II Kings 25:13-17] of items from the Tabernacle of Moshe our Teacher.
20.1: (2) THE TABERNACLE OF THE PACT.  It [Scripture] recounts the superior qualities of the Tabernacle, for which it could remain permanent and not fall into the enemy's hands.  First, that it was the Tabernacle of the Pact, that the Tablets of the Pact were in it.  Second, that it was "drawn up at Moshe's bidding."  Third, that it was the responsibility of the Levites under the direction of Itamar, for in fact the responsibility for all parts of the Tabernacle was under Itamar.   Fourth (v.22), "Now Bezalel, son of Uri son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, had made," for the chief artisans of the Tabernacle and its vessels were among the elite and the righteous of the generation, and so the Sh'china rested on what they made, and it did not fall into the enemy's hands.  But Shlomo's Temple, for which those who did the work were from Tyre, even though the Sh'china rested on it, its components deteriorated, and it was necessary to do restorative work, and it ultimately fell into the enemy's hands.  But the Second Temple, which lacked all of these attributes, the Sh'china did not rest on it, and it fell into the enemy's hands.  For indeed, the Second Temple was not the Tabernacle of the Pact, for the Tablets of the Pact were not there, and it was "drawn up" only at Koresh's bidding, and the Levites were not there [at the construction], as Ezra testified when he said (Ezra 8:15), "I reviewed the people and the priests, but I did not find any Levites there," and among those who engaged in its construction, there were Sidonites and Tyrites, as is explained in the Book of Ezra.
